_comment: Romance, rivalries and friendships (issue #116, DESIGN.md 5.10), read by scripts/relationships.gd. ROMANCE: the characters under romance.cast can fall for Ash. After their rank 3 scene, once their bond reaches romance.moment_points, they want a word again: the 'moment' scene (an evening, lighter than the rank scenes), whose choices carry romance true (Ash says yes: the bond turns romantic) or false (Ash stays a friend; the question is never asked again). The rank 4 scene waits until the moment is seen. One romance at a time: picking romance while Ash is with someone else ends that one (the label says so first). An ended romance costs the ex romance.ended_bond points (never below their rank), plays their 'ended' lines the next time Ash talks to them in Hollowmark, and can't be rekindled. While a romance is on: the partner's 'perk' counts like a bond perk (effect keys as in data/bonds.json), their daily chat in Hollowmark uses 'talk' lines, and their rank 5 scene is 'rank5' instead of the one in bonds.json. Lines are [speaker, text] or [speaker, text, expression], speaker '' = narration; Ash never speaks. PAIRS: two people who get on (friends) or can't stand each other (rivals). Posted together = both in the party, both staff in the same building, or on the same expedition. effects: expedition (success chance, %), building (added to the building's staff output, in the units the building counts), party ({damage, hp, guard (share of damage taken away; negative = more damage taken), power_rate, revive}), bond (bond points with Ash for each of them per day posted together; never below their rank). banter: two-line exchanges, one played at the start of a mission they are both on, and quoted in expedition reports. Rivals with a truce make peace after truce.days days posted together; the truce then replaces their name, text, effects and banter.

perk.name: Leading Lady
perk.desc: Fallen party members get back up 25% faster on missions.

moment.title: Second Billing
lines: Late. The Encore's old dressing-room trunk stands open in the barracks loft. Fauvette has hung a sheet for a curtain and lit exactly one candle.
velvette
Sit. No, there. That is the good side of the candle. I gave you the good side. Notice it.
velvette
I've been thinking about what you did. Not looking away. Rare, that. Everyone looks away from me eventually. It's practically my exit cue.
velvette
So here is my problem, darling. I don't do sincere. Sincere has no second act. Et pourtant.
She tips her head. The candle does a great deal for her eyeliner, and she knows it.
velvette
I am offering you a part. Small, demanding, terrible hours. Leading man, if you want it. Or you stay my favourite audience and I never ask again. Both honourable. One more fun.

choice.label: [Take the part: kiss her]
reply: House rules. Nobody hears about this. Everybody will guess. I deny it beautifully.
She pinches out the candle. Whatever happens next happens offstage, where it belongs.

choice.label: [Applaud softly, and stay in your seat]
reply: Front row, then. Best seat in the house, and you never have to learn any lines. Wise.
Don't look so worried. I'm not wounded. I am a professional. I will be wounded in private, with a bottle, like an artist.

rank5.title: Curtain Call
lines: velvette
The Gilded Heron had a full house. I came on during the closing act. In costume, naturellement. One has standards.
velvette
I challenged Augustin with the whole Marsh watching. He'd never held a sword in his life. I let him keep his. Then I read the commissions aloud. Every name. Every price.
velvette
Eleven names, read slow. And the audience didn't cheer. They took their hats off. Best show I ever gave.
velvette
And through all of it I kept finding you in the wings. So distracting. I nearly missed a cue. I never miss a cue.
velvette
House rules: a secret for a secret. I owe you one since the first night.
She leans in and says it in Ash's ear: her real name. It is a very ordinary name. Nobody else will ever hear it.
velvette
That's what you call me when it's just us. In public I am still Fauvette, and you are still my extremely lucky stagehand.
velvette
Played a hundred lovers. Every one died in the third act. I want one where nobody does.

choice.label: [Say nothing, and kiss her]
reply: That's the trouble with a silent leading man. I have to read everything in the eyes. Luckily, I'm fluent.

choice.label: [Keep her name, and her hand]
reply: Look at you, keeping secrets. I've corrupted you completely. Good. Don't you dare sell that one.

ended: Oh, don't creep up on me looking tragic. I heard. Everybody heard. I made sure the version going round is the one where I left you.
No hard feelings. A few soft ones, which I keep in a drawer with the other props. Exit stage left, darling.
talk: Stop looking at me like that in public. Save it for private, where it counts.
I've rewritten my memoirs. You're in chapter nine. It's very flattering. Mostly to me.
If anyone asks, you're my bodyguard. If anyone asks the bodyguard, the bodyguard says nothing. You're perfect for the role.
Rapier lesson tonight. You'll lose. I'll gloat. It'll be the highlight of both our days.

moment.title: Rooftop Rates
lines: Past midnight. Jessamy has found the one roof in Hollowmark with a view of nothing in particular, and a blanket she definitely didn't buy.
jessamy
Shh. Listen. That's the best sound in the world. Nobody lookin' for anybody.
jessamy
I've been doin' sums. You never ask what's in the crates, you never ask where I go, and you stood in front of the sun for me. That's three favours. I hate owin'.
jessamy
So. I can pay you back in coin, which I've nicked. Or in Supplies, which I've also nicked.
She shuffles closer on the tiles, all elbows, until her shoulder is against Ash's. Solid, at this hour.
jessamy
Or I could stop pretendin' I climb up here for the view. Your call. I'm very bad at waitin', so call fast.

choice.label: [Pull the blanket round you both]
reply: Oh. Oh, that was the right answer. That was so much the right answer.
Don't tell anyone. Smuggler's honour. I've got a reputation for no attachments, and it's been very good for business.
They stay until the sky starts to grey. She doesn't fade. Not tonight. She checks twice, and laughs both times.

choice.label: [Toss her an apple: call it even]
reply: Ha! Paid in fruit. Fair. Generous, even.
Partners, then. The business kind. Best kind, honestly. Nobody gets their heart nicked, only the cargo.

rank5.title: Noon
lines: It is noon. The plaza is full of honest people doing honest things. In the middle of it, Jessamy lies flat on her back on the cobbles, eyes shut, perfectly solid.
jessamy
Don't block it. Shift. You're in my sun.
jessamy
Fennick wrote me back in. Took him an hour, his hand was shakin' so bad. When he asked for my occupation, I told him to put "yes".
jessamy
Then he asked for next of kin. I gave him your name. He said you haven't got one. I said write "Ash" and stop being difficult.
jessamy
So you're on my line now. Official. Sorry. Should've asked. Wasn't goin' to.
jessamy
Lie down. Properly. Next to me. I want to know what it's like holdin' someone's hand in daylight and actually feelin' it.
Ash lies down. Her hand is warm and very solid and slightly sticky from something she lifted off a pie stall.
jessamy
There. That's it? That's what everyone else gets all the time? Unbelievable. You lot have been keepin' this very quiet.

choice.label: [Squeeze her hand]
reply: I felt that. I felt that. Do it again. ...Again. I'm going to be insufferable about this for years.

choice.label: [Put your hat over both your faces]
reply: Ha! Now nobody can see. Which means I can do this.
Under the hat, in the middle of the noon plaza, she kisses Ash like she's settling a very old account.

ended: So that's how it is. No, it's fine. I'm a smuggler. I know when a cargo's gone to another buyer.
I'll still run your supplies. I'll just charge you for the rooftop. Backdated. With interest.
talk: Saved you a pear. Don't ask whose orchard.
Roof, later. Bring nothing. Bring yourself. ...That came out soppier than I planned.
I told Tobble you're my business partner. He laughed so hard he had to sit down.
I can see you in daylight now. Properly. You've got a freckle, there. I'm keeping it.

moment.title: Off the Books
lines: The Command Table, after hours. Odile has two cups, a pot of something strong and a ledger she has very deliberately closed.
odile
I am not working. Look. Closed. I am being informal. I read about it.
odile
I have drawn up a statement. Of you. Assets: you listen. You sat with me. You do not round anything off, not even people.
odile
Liabilities: no Ledger line, no surname, no fixed abode, and you keep walking into the Blank on purpose. Any assessor would tell me to walk away.
She turns her cup a quarter turn, then back. Then a quarter turn again.
odile
I am proposing a joint account. Emotionally. I am aware that is the least romantic sentence ever spoken in the Inklands. I had a better one. I crossed it out.

choice.label: [Take her hand across the ledger]
reply: I shall have to declare it. To myself. Privately. In red ink, because red is for the things that matter.
She doesn't let go of Ash's hand to pour the second cup. She pours it badly, and for once doesn't fix it.

choice.label: [Raise your cup to her: colleagues]
reply: Colleagues. Of course. Very sensible. I should have advised the same.
Thank you for not making me read the crossed-out one. Same time tomorrow? Strictly the accounts.

rank5.title: Reconciled
lines: odile
She came alone. No guards, no clerks. Older than I remembered. She'd brought her own pen this time.
odile
We argued in numbers for three hours. Then I audited her, right there in the inn, on the back of the menu.
odile
Every account balanced but one line, twenty-six years old. Ninety Gilt, quietly moved, to keep one village off the lists. Penhallow Mere. Where I was born.
odile
She said, "Keep the ledger. Use it better than I did." Then she asked about you.
odile

I said you have no name, no income and you fight the end of the world for a living. She said it was the most Penhallow thing she had ever heard. I believe that was approval. She does not use that column much.
Odile turns Ash's account page around. Under Liabilities, everything is struck through. Under Assets there is one new line, in red: ODILE. Then, smaller, in her most careful hand: (jointly held).

choice.label: [Initial the page, next to her name]
reply: Countersigned. Binding. You are stuck with me. That is how accounts work.
...That's also how this works. I checked.

choice.label: [Kiss her ink-stained knuckles]
reply: Do it again. I want to be sure I record it accurately.

ended: I have closed the account. Don't. It is entered properly: one item, written off. Not lost. Written off. There is a difference, and I am holding on to it.
We shall work together. Professionally. I am very good at professionally. I have had years of practice.
talk: I've moved you from "contingent" to "recurring". It's a big step. Don't make it weird.
You were reckless out there today. I've made a note. A fond note. Still a note.
Supper at eight. I've budgeted for wine. One bottle. Two if the Fray's down.
My mother wrote. She wants to know your intentions. I told her they're none of her business and entirely honourable.

perk.name: Watch Your Six
perk.desc: The party takes 5% less damage on missions.

moment.title: Off Duty
lines: Behind the Barracks. Daro is sharpening a blade that's already sharp, which is how you know they want company.
ninefingers
Sit down, you're blocking my light. ...No, stay. That was an order. Allowed to give them now. Officially dead.
ninefingers
Here's the thing. I don't do this. In the army you don't get attached to whoever's next to you. They get moved, or struck off, or you do.
ninefingers
Then you put your hand on my shoulder and I didn't flinch. Always flinch. Been annoyed about it for days.
They set the whetstone down. Nine fingers, laced together, very still.
ninefingers
So I'm asking. Plainly, because I'm bad at the other way. You and me. Not as a unit. As a... you know. Don't make me say the word, Unwritten.

choice.label: [Lean in and kiss them]
reply: Anyone in the Barracks finds out, I'll deny it, then run them round the yard till they forget.
Daro picks the whetstone back up. They don't sharpen anything with it. The other hand stays in Ash's.

choice.label: [Sit back to back with them, the way soldiers do]
reply: Back to back. Yeah. That I know how to do.
Honest answer. Good. Never mention this again, and you're still on watch with me tonight.

rank5.title: Roll of Honour
lines: ninefingers
It's there. Whole village. Mill's turning. Kids. Goats. Bad beer.
ninefingers
And in the chapel, a plaque. "Corporal Daro, fallen against the Blank." Concord declared me dead so they wouldn't have to say deserted.
ninefingers
Forty civvies pray for me every week. Didn't have the heart to correct them.
ninefingers
Stood in that chapel and thought: dead me's got a plaque. What's the live one got?
ninefingers
Then thought about you. Embarrassing. In a chapel. With goats watching.

choice.label: [Count their fingers with them: nine. Keep hold of the hand]
reply: Nine. Yeah. Nine's what it cost. And look what it bought.

choice.label: [Salute. Then kiss them anyway]
reply: Stop that. ...Fine. Back at you, Unwritten. Both parts.

ended: Heard the news. Don't. Been struck off worse lists than yours.
Still got your back in the field. Not up for negotiation. The rest is dismissed, soldier.
talk: You took a hit for me yesterday. Don't. That's my job. ...Thanks.
The recruits think we're plotting something. Let them. Keeps them sharp.
Nine fingers, and one of them always ends up holding your hand. Maths is weird.
Bad dream last night. The forms again. You were there, tearing them up. Better than the usual ending.

perk.name: Bouncer's Favourite
perk.desc: +10 max HP for the party on missions.

moment.title: After Hours
lines: Closing time at Tobble's. Ottoline is stacking chairs, two at a time, then three, then giving up and carrying the table.
ottoline
You're still here. Everyone's gone. That's usually when I throw folk out.
ottoline
Thirty year on doors, counting the Encore. Know what you learn? Who stays after the lights go up. Drunks. Thieves. Folk who want summat.
ottoline
You stood by me at that door like it were nowt. Like you'd do it every night. Nobody does that.
She puts the table down very carefully, as if it might be the thing that breaks.
ottoline
So I'm asking once, and if it's no, we laugh about it and you help with the chairs. Do you want to stay after closing? Not tonight. Generally.

choice.label: [Stay. Take her hand]
reply: Ha! Right. Good. Had a speech ready for no. It were very dignified.
House rules still apply. Nobody touches you while I'm about. That goes double now.
She hugs Ash off the floor, reorganising several bones, and then, much more gently, sets Ash back down.

choice.label: [Pick up a chair and start stacking]
reply: No, I mean it. Not many'd say no to my face. Mind your fingers on that one, it bites.

rank5.title: Coat Check
lines: Ottoline comes in out of the weather, soaked to the skin, carrying six coats over her arm like sleeping children.
ottoline
It were the door. Just the door, stood in the white, nowt round it. My chalk marks still on the frame.
ottoline
I knocked back. Six times. Then I opened it. Nowt behind it but the cloakroom. Six coats on six hooks, waiting to be collected.
ottoline
So I collected them. You hand the ticket over, you get your coat, you go home. They're on the old tree in the plaza.
ottoline
On the walk home I worked summat out. Six year I've held a door shut. Never once thought about who I'd open one for.
ottoline
Turns out I know. It's right annoying. You've got a face like a closed sign and I'm mad about it.

choice.label: [Hand her a fresh stick of chalk]
reply: For the list? No. You don't go on the list. You go on the door. Top of it, where everyone can see.

choice.label: [Hold the door open, and follow her in]
reply: Ha! Manners. Get in, then, before I change my mind. I won't. Be quick anyway.

ended: Right. Well. That's the door shut, then. I'm good with shut doors. Had practice.
Nobody lays a finger on you while I'm about. That rule stays. The rest, you can stack your own chairs.
talk: Kept your seat warm. By sitting in it. Shift.
Tobble asked my intentions. I said honourable and very large. He went a funny colour.
Anyone gives you trouble, you point. I'll do the rest. That's romance, that is.
Brought you soup. Didn't make it. Threatened the man who did.

perk.name: Dance Card
perk.desc: Every standing gain with a faction is 1 bigger.

moment.title: The Balcony
lines: Hollowmark has no balconies, so Hortense has taken the top of the town hall stairs, opened the window and called it one.
hortense
On the Causeway, this is where it happens. The ball goes on inside. Two people step out for air, and come back in with a story.
hortense
I have stepped out for air with half the Concord's nobility. I always came back in with the story and they came back in poorer.
hortense
This time I would rather not come back in at all. Which is the most inconvenient thing that has ever happened to me.
She turns her mask over in her hands, the velvet one from the masquerade. She does not put it on.
hortense
So. A dance, sweet, and we see where it goes. Or a bow, and we go back to being excellent friends who flirt. I shall be charming about either. I am always charming.

choice.label: [Take the dance]
reply: ...You lead with the left. I taught you that. I did not teach you the rest.
Not a word of this downstairs. I have a reputation for breaking hearts and I mean to keep it.
The window stays open. The draught gets in, and neither of them closes it.

choice.label: [Bow, and kiss her hand]
reply: Ah. Gallant, and final. That is the nicest refusal I have ever had, and I have had a few.
Excellent friends who flirt, then. I shall make it the best friendship on the Causeway. Everyone will be jealous.

rank5.title: One True Thing
lines: Hollowmark is quiet. Bérénice de Saulx is asleep in the town hall with six other girls, under every blanket Hollowmark owns.
hortense
She asked me who you were. I said you were the person who does not exist. She said that was silly, because she could see you, and because I keep looking at you.
hortense
I have lied to everyone I have ever met, beautifully, for a living. You made it impossible. I have stopped minding.
hortense
So. One true thing. I love you, and I would like to stay. There. It has no French in it. I checked twice.

choice.label: [Kiss her]
reply: Mm. The Causeway would call that a scandal. I call it a very good evening.

choice.label: [Take both her hands]
reply: Careful, sweet. If you keep doing that I shall have to start telling the truth on purpose.

ended: I heard. Of course I heard: I hear everything, it was my profession. Do not look at me like a dropped glass.
I shall tell the Causeway I left you. They will believe it. They always believe the de Saulx. We will still dance at weddings.
talk: If anyone asks, I am here for the politics. Nobody will believe me. That is the fun of it.
I wrote to Bérénice about you. She wrote back one word: 'finally'. Children are very rude.
You still never look at your feet when we dance. I adore that. Also you have stepped on mine twice.
On the Causeway, a lady keeps three lovers and a duelling partner. I have rationalised. You are all four.

perk.name: Love Song
perk.desc: The party's gauge fills 10% faster on missions.

moment.title: Duet
lines: Late, in the tavern's back room. Saffron has a borrowed fiddle across her knees and no intention of playing it.
saffron
Here's a thing. I write songs about everyone. Bran's got one, it's mostly about his arms. Tobble's got three, all rude.
saffron
Yours keeps going wrong. It starts off a funny one, about the quiet sort. Then it turns into a love song by the second verse, every time. I've tried. It won't stay funny.
saffron
So I'm asking, love, before I make a fool of myself in front of a paying crowd. Is it a love song, or do I keep trying to make it a funny one?

choice.label: [Kiss her]
reply: ...Love song. Right. That settles the second verse.
Don't tell anyone. They'll all want one, and I've only got the one voice.
She puts the fiddle down. Somewhere a lamp lights itself that nobody sang.

choice.label: [Laugh, and point to the funny bits]
reply: Funny one it is. Good. Funny songs get more applause anyway.
Mates, then. Best kind of harmony. Nobody goes flat.

rank5.title: The Whole Song
lines: saffron
She came out, love. She came out, and she was cross, because I'd left the kettle on eleven years ago.
saffron
The house is gone now. It went when the song went, like songs do. Mam's at the tavern telling Tobble he's watering the gin, and he is.
saffron
I finished a song. First one ever. I thought it'd feel like dying. It felt like getting off a stage and you're there with my coat.
saffron
And I've finished yours. The love song. Every verse. I'm going to sing it to you, all the way to the end, and you're going to stay. That's what finished means.

choice.label: [Listen to every verse]
reply: ...And nothing went away. Look at that. You're still here.

choice.label: [Join in on the last line]
reply: Flat! Brave! Perfect. That's our duet, that is.

ended: So that's that. I've cut your verses out of the love song. It's a lot shorter now. Funnier, too.
No hard feelings, love. Well. Some. They'll make a good song one day.
talk: I sang your name at the window this morning and a sparrow came out of the last note. It's still on the sill. I've been feeding it crumbs, so that's the two of us responsible for a sparrow now.
Mam says you're too quiet. I said that's the point. She said 'oh' in her worst voice.
Every song I write's about you now. It's very bad for business. Nobody wants a sad song about mud any more.
Come and sit at the front tonight. I like to know where you are when I hit the high bits.

pairs.name: Old Encore hands
pairs.text: Ottoline keeps the door, Fauvette works the room. Fifteen years of closing nights between them.
banter: Ottoline, chérie, if this goes badly, carry me out dramatically.
I carry you out every time. You always want it dramatic, you.
Same as the Encore. I hit them, you charm the ones I miss.
You never miss. It's very bad for my part.

pairs.name: Night owls
pairs.text: Jessamy and Fauvette know every back door that's open after dark, and who left it open.
banter: Bet you a crate of Coven gin I get more of 'em.
Darling, I'd never bet against you. I'd only cheat.
I know. I can see my own feet. It's horrible.

pairs.name: Two sets of books
pairs.text: Odile and Quill argue about rounding for hours, and between them nothing gets past.
banter: I rounded it beautifully. There's a difference.
Should we tell Ash we've found eleven Gilt in the drains column?
Twelve. And no. Let it be a nice surprise.

pairs.name: Old soldiers
pairs.text: Bran and Daro cover each other's blind side without being asked. Neither will admit it.
banter: Saw it. Your left, mercenary. Your other left.
What's your rate for this one?
Double. I'm workin' with you. That's 'azard pay.

pairs.name: Two ex-Concord
pairs.text: Quill and Daro both walked out on the Concord, and know exactly where its forms are weakest.
banter: Form Nine-B. Requisition of a deserter's remains.
Fill it in. Tell them they can collect when I'm done with them.

pairs.name: On speaking terms with the dead
pairs.text: Pell and Hild both talk to the dead. The dead give them directions.
banter: They say left at the old well, Sister.
Mine say right. Mine are more polite about it, though.

pairs.name: Family, probably
pairs.text: Tobble's niece, or cousin, or creditor. Nobody remembers, least of all them. Work goes faster when they're shouting at each other fondly.
banter: Mind your back, lass. You're not getting any younger.
Neither are you, and you've been retiring since before I were born.

pairs.name: Maps and back roads
pairs.text: Hetty draws the roads a week before they exist. Jessamy has already used them.
banter: There's a road here on Thursday. Bearing north-north-east.
Lovely. I'll be on it Wednesday night.

pairs.name: The bar tab
pairs.text: Quill has kept Tobble's bar tab for nine years. Tobble disputes every line of it.
banter: That goose left of its own free will.
Bookkeeper's got a face like a closed till.
And you've a tab like an open wound.

truce.name: Tab settled
truce.text: Quill and Tobble agreed the tab at last: forty Gilt, or one very good bottle. The bottle was opened. The figure is never to be mentioned again.
banter: I've a new column for you, Tobble. "Forgiven".
Put it next to "owed to me". It's longer.

pairs.name: The bandage bill
pairs.text: Gristle bills Bran for every bandage. Bran refuses to pay on principle, and gets hurt on purpose to spite her.
banter: Every scratch goes on your account, dearie.
Then I'll bleed quietly, out of principle.
You overcharged me for the last stitch.
You screamed for the last stitch. Screaming costs extra, it does.

truce.name: Account in good standing
truce.text: Bran paid his bill. All of it, in coin, with a little bow. Gristle has framed the receipt. They are still rude to each other, but now it's a hobby.
banter: Account's paid, so I'll patch you for free today. Don't get used to it.
Free? Now I'm worried. What's in it?

pairs.name: Tax and contraband
pairs.text: Odile keeps assessing Jessamy's crates. Jessamy keeps emptying them before Odile can finish the sum.
banter: Nothin' taxable. Mostly air. Very fine, imported air.
She's followin' me with a pencil. It's unsettlin'.
I am following the money. You keep getting in the way.

truce.name: Off the record
truce.text: Odile and Jessamy have reached an understanding: Odile doesn't ask what's in the crates, and Jessamy brings her one, unopened, every week. It's always a good pen.
banter: I am not asking what is in the crate.
And I'm not telling you it's the nib you wanted.

pairs.name: Collector and deserter
pairs.text: Daro tore up an order to strike a village. Odile used to deliver them. Both quit. Neither has forgiven the other for having been there first.
banter: How many villages did you collect, ma'am?
Fewer than your regiment struck out, Corporal.
You had a choice. You tore it up.
So did you. Took the ledger. We're both thieves. Get over it.

truce.name: Same side of the ledger
truce.text: Somewhere on the road Daro and Odile compared notes, and found they had both been lied to by the same three men. They are making a list. It is not a kind list.
banter: Lieutenant Garrow. The Assessor-General. Whoever invented Form Nine-B.

pairs.name: Debtor and collector
pairs.text: Every debt Dunmore owes is tattooed on him. Odile can't stop adding it up, out loud, while he works.
banter: Your left shoulder alone comes to four hundred Gilt.
My left shoulder's not for sale, miss, if it please you.

truce.name: A payment plan
truce.text: Odile drew up a payment plan for Dunmore's back, shoulder and most of one leg. He cried a little. It's the first plan anyone's ever made him.
banter: Paid off another elbow this week, miss.
Good. Ahead of schedule. I am very proud. Professionally.

pairs.name: One spotlight
pairs.text: Fauvette and the Merrow Three both expect the last word. There are four of them and only one last word.
banter: Darlings, a little harmony goes a long way. Ideally away.
WE WERE SINGING IN THE MARGINS BEFORE YOU HAD TEETH, MY BIRD.

truce.name: A duet, for once
truce.text: Fauvette and the Merrow Three found a song they all know: the Encore's old closing number. Now they do it together, in four parts. Pim gets the high bit.
banter: FROM THE TOP, FAUVETTE? PROPER THIS TIME.
From the top, mes petites. Pim, the high bit is yours.

pairs.name: The Coven grudge
pairs.text: Mother Gristle left the Coven over a bill nobody paid. Mr. Biscuits was the Coven's dog at the time, and remembers whose side he was on.
banter: Keep that animal off my bottles.
Grr. (He would like it known that he is not an animal. He is a familiar. With a pedigree.)

truce.name: Treats on account
truce.text: Gristle started keeping a jar of biscuits by her bottles. She bills them to Ash, naturally. Mr. Biscuits considers the matter closed.
banter: One biscuit. One. Two coppers on Ash's account, that is.

pairs.name: The good chair
pairs.text: Bran's contract says he gets the good chair. Ottoline throws people out of chairs for a living. Furniture is suffering.
banter: Your chair's about to go through a window, Tolley.
Bet I drop more of them than you.
Bet you need carrying home after.

truce.name: Two chairs
truce.text: Ottoline built a second good chair out of a wardrobe and a Concord desk. It is enormous. Bran pretends to hate it and sits in it every night.
banter: Course it is. Built it to hold me.

pairs.name: Two rapiers
pairs.text: A marquise and a showgirl, both with swords and both used to being the only one in the room. Fauvette calls Hortense 'the amateur'. Hortense calls Fauvette 'the cabaret girl', which is worse.
banter: The marquise holds her sword like a fan, chérie. Very pretty. Very slow.
And Fauvette holds hers like a bouquet she expects to be thrown. Everyone has their gifts.
Shall we count, sweet? First to five.
Darling, I stopped counting at eleven.

truce.name: A shared bow
truce.text: Hortense and Fauvette fought a practice bout in the practice yard that went on for an hour and ended in a draw neither will admit to. They now take the same corner of the tavern and criticise everyone else's footwork.
banter: You left your guard open on the third pass, marquise.
I know. I wanted to see if you would notice. You did. How irritating.

pairs.name: Cabaret hours
pairs.text: For years Saffron sang at the Gilt Lantern on Lantern Quay and Ottoline kept the Encore's door at Gallows Ferry. The same drunks did the rounds of both, and the two of them have a hundred stories about them.
banter: Ottoline, remember the magistrate at the Lantern? The one who sang along?
I remember. I threw him out by the second chorus. You thanked me.
You sing, I hit. Like the old days.
Like the old days, love. Except now the drunks have teeth.

pairs.name: Small print
pairs.text: Bran's contract is on his arm and Nan's is in a moneylender's box. They spend whole evenings reading each other's clauses out loud and laughing at the worst ones.
banter: Bran, what's the small print on your arm say again?
So does your arm, sunshine. Yours just uses clauses.

pairs.name: Creative accounting
pairs.text: Quill cooks the books for Hollowmark and Nan cooks them for herself. Each is sure the other is skimming. Both are right.
banter: Nan, the supply ledger is six Gilt short.
Is it? Funny. My purse is six Gilt heavy. Must be a draught.
Quill, sunshine, you've carried a two there that wants to be a seven.
I've carried it exactly where I wanted it, thank you.

truce.name: Two sets of books
truce.text: Quill and Nan agreed to audit each other weekly. Hollowmark's books have never been cleaner, and the two of them have never been happier about it.
banter: I found your six Gilt, Nan.
And I found your seven. Call it square?
